entries.body:
Got stuck in Loganville for the weekend — the weather was awful — it blew & rained on Saturday, then rained all Sunday. The Rally hype was intense — all these boaters talking themselves into going to sea. Talked to Tranquility & Silverfin Monday morning — they were in Peterson Bay so we went up there. There we finally met Indulgence II with Mike, Elke and Ben; also Julia with Larry & Ken; and Overproof with Virginia & Derek. We had seen these boats since Fiji!

Brian was happy to hang out with Ben, or Larry from Julia, those guys are big boys! We had a wonderful time there, dinghying to the Blue Hole, diving the crashed airplane on the reef, partying with the other boats. Just before they were planning to leave for Australia last Thursday, Ben was jumping off our spreaders with Brian, slipped, and fell on the life lines, gashed his head on the toerail. He looked pretty beat up at first. Got an ambulance and got him to the hospital. Luckily, he only needed some stitches in his forehead. He was back the next day, feeling fine. So, we stayed too, spent a lot of time with Indulgence & Julia.

Finally got out of Peterson Bay on Monday, went down to Palikulo Bay. Had a blast exploring the freighter beached there, swimming in the clear water. Hung out with Carl & Kathleen on Silverfin for the day. Hated to leave! But it is time to go on now — 2 weeks of light winds ahead and Chesterfield Reef beckoned. We have 10–12 knots of wind from the SE, we are still sailing along the south coast of Espiritu Santo. Goodbye Vanuatu — it has been a memorable two months!
entries.conditions: Departed Luganville / Palikulo for Australia via Chesterfield. Wind: SE 10–12 knots.

entries.body: Well it could be worse! Last night was peaceful after we poled out the genoa, moving at 4½ knots, wind backed to the east. This morning the wind almost died completely, we were bouncing along at 1½ knots for a while. Not thrilling, but better than nothing. The wind came back this afternoon, 8–10 knots and we are moving smoothly at 5 knots with four sails up. Nice sailing! We expected very light winds for this trip, want to get to Chesterfield and enjoy a few calm days there before the last leg back to a continent.
entries.conditions: Wind: east then light, later 8–10 knots; 5 knots with four sails. 24-hour run — 105 miles.

entries.body: Beautiful night last night, charging along up to 6 knots at times with 4 sails up, following the path made by the extremely bright crescent moon. It was quite comfortable — we are all enjoying this sail. Talked to Indulgence & Julia this morning. Lost a big fish along with the lure, Thomas is hungry for something different. He ate enough oysters and coconut crabs in Peterson Bay!
entries.conditions: Up to 6 knots with 4 sails. 24-hour run — 115 miles.

entries.body: Another nice night, but sunrise brought light winds. It was hot, progress slow, boat didn't steer well. Finally got a bit more wind late in afternoon. Caught a huge mahi just after sunrise.
entries.conditions: Light winds after sunrise. 24-hour run — 117 miles.

entries.body:
Not a very exciting day — been almost becalmed most of it. Trying to get the boat going again now, before sunset. Morale is good, however!

Oh — had some hitch hikers last night! A tired booby landed on the mizzen boom just after sunset. He was no problem — his ass was hanging over the water, but then his buddies landed on the spreaders and all of a sudden there was bird shit all over the place. Thomas chased them off, but the first one stayed until sunrise.
Today is flat calm, oily sea, totally hazy gray horizon, no visibility. We play with the sails and then get tired of it. Very hot, good day to do laundry!

Wind came back late yesterday afternoon with a bang! Within an hour we had the main down, mizzen reefed, furled genoa. It blew like stink all night — 30–35 knots from the south. It was relatively calm north of Chesterfield Reef, which we passed in the middle of the night. No stopping at uncharted reefs in this weather! Finally switched to staysail to try to slow the boat down. Overproof and Indulgence II got nailed too, after us. Very uncomfortable ride — food flying all over the place. Being becalmed sounds good now! Will head to Frederick Reef now and stop there.
entries.conditions: Wind: S 30–35 knots; passed Chesterfield Reef at night. 24-hour run — 135 miles.

entries.body: Today has been an exhilarating day — blue sky, big waves, lots of whitecaps. 30 knots of wind. Keep trying to slow the boat down, it is impossible. Running 5½–6 under staysail only. Not so uncomfortable as yesterday. It is possible to stand on deck without getting wet. We will be at Frederick Cay Reef before sunrise tomorrow. Looking forward to peaceful anchorage in clear blue water, a sandy beach.
entries.conditions: Wind: 30 knots; 5½–6 under staysail. Bound Frederick Reef. 24-hour run — 145 miles.

entries.body: Arrived at Frederick Reef Thurs at sunrise, anchored just before the Namba Net at 8 am. Not exactly a calm anchorage! The boat pitched and rolled, too rough to get off or swim, still blowing 20+. We had reduced to bare poles before sunrise and were still doing 3–4 knots. Indulgence II arrived at 10pm, rather frazzled from navigating into the reef in the dark. Had a fun day yesterday — hanging out on the coral rubble hump that stuck out of the sea at high tide, then had beers and dinner on Indulgence. Figured out a new way to hoist the dinghy aboard last night, with the staysail halyard. Left at 7 this morning, 15–20 SE wind, hard on it heading 195° to Bundaberg. It's a beautiful day; just wish the wind was more easterly. As long as it stays where it is and we can hold the course, no problem.
entries.conditions: Frederick Reef layover; departed for Bundaberg. Wind: SE 15–20, hard on it, course 195°.

entries.body: What a nice night, full moon, light winds, calm seas, very comfortable. We made lots of southing, can just hold our course today. Were doing 7 knots for awhile! Hope the wind holds & doesn't turn more south.
entries.conditions: Light winds; up to 7 knots. 24-hour run — 140 miles.

stops.name: Bundaberg, Fraser Island & Tin Can Bay

entries.body:
We arrived in Bundaberg Monday morning at sunrise, had to slow down some once we passed the reef. There were 20 boats ahead of us awaiting checkin! Got through by 4pm, piece of cake. Relaxed with Indulgence II. Bundaberg river entrance was not particularly thrilling — very flat, ugly gray water, poisonous sea snakes. We went up river to the town with Virginia on Overproof for a few days, to do some shopping. Bundaberg was neat and clean, everything available. The men walk around in Crocodile Dundee outfits, and the women are scantily dressed. Very redneck. Spent a couple more days at the mouth of the river, until Julia with Ken & Larry showed up. Left Mon the 17th for Fraser Island — what a great spot! It was paradise there — miles of white sand beaches, crystal clear water, birds. But the wind turned NW and we had to get out. Too bad — it would have been perfect for windsurfing in the lagoon. Spent the next few days traveling south in the Great Sandy Straits. Great sailing in flat water, but the NW winds made anchoring uncomfortable. Finally found some protection in Gary's Anchorage. Came down to Tin Can Bay yesterday, just before the wind turned south again. Anchored in the river here, quite a way from town, but it's peaceful. Lots of sand bars, sleepy little town. Overproof is here, mostly Aussie boats. Will be stuck until wind turns NE again.

Bundaberg highlights: nasty thick gray sea snakes, 1000's of bats flying across the river at sunset. Yucky water!
entries.conditions: Arrived Bundaberg; later Fraser Island, Great Sandy Strait, Garry's Anchorage (written Gary's), Tin Can Bay. Wind: NW then south.

entries.body: Enjoyed our week in Tin Can Bay — we met Virginia on Overproof there and she arranged a trip to a National Forest and a hike to Lake Boona with some friends of hers. It was beautiful — huge old Kauri trees towering out of sight, thousands of birds. I had a refreshing swim in the fresh water lake. Tin Can Bay was very quiet, but people were friendly, and internet at the library was free. The dinghy ride was a bit long and wet. Mostly only Australian boats around. We spent one day at Inskip Point, and walked part of the endless windward beach. Today we left at 4:30 to sail down to Mooloolaba, 60 miles. Not a lot of wind in the morning, but it picked up to 15 in the afternoon. The bar crossing to offshore was crazy — 20 boats next to each other, motoring through 6ft swells, trying to get out. What a zoo! But of course eventually they all passed Charlotte. We got in and were anchored by 4, found a nice hole to sit in. Very suburban here — fancy huge holiday houses along the waterfront.
entries.conditions: Tin Can Bay via Inskip Point to Mooloolaba, 60 miles. Wind light then 15; rough bar exit.

entries.body: A month went by quickly in Mooloolaba! I guess we were comfortable there. It took a while to get used to the scene, but we enjoyed afternoons on the beach, with Brian on his boogie board. He really got into it! Suleika with Martin, Katherine and 8-yr-old [illegible], showed up, so we decided to spend Christmas with them. It was a fun day, spent time on the beach as usual. Brian drove us crazy wanting things. Got into exercising every morning, running, working out at an exercise site. Silent Runner came through a few days before Christmas, also Tranquility. We went to the Australia Zoo and saw crocodiles, kangaroos, and koalas, also many snakes, poisonous & pythons. We saw the last Lord of the Rings movie. Got used to the yuppie-tourist atmosphere but then the water cops came around and bugged us to move on. Indulgence & Julia arrived, but they were disappointing — too involved in each other. It was a fun month, but time to move on. Today winds are light and we took all day to get 40 miles south to Tangalooma, on Moreton Island. We saw Desert Rose sailing north to Mooloolaba — what a shame to miss them by a day!
entries.conditions: After ~1 month at Mooloolaba; sailed ~40 miles to Tangalooma, Moreton Island. Light winds.

entries.body:
After a morning of school work, we decided to move on as the anchorage was getting rolly. Today is great sailing — downwind with the genoa poled out. Only 20 miles to Peel Island where we will wait out the NW flow. We meet up with Virginia on Overproof here — lots of boats, but it is a big bay, long sandy beach. Thomas is trying windsurfing here.

p.s. — New Years Eve in Mooloolaba was fantastic — lots of fireworks on the beach, some in a boat out on the water. It was a sight with the lights on the crashing surf, fireworks shooting into the waves. The Australians worked very hard at getting drunk, what a scene.
entries.conditions: Tangalooma to Peel Island, ~20 miles. Downwind, genoa poled out; waiting out NW flow.

entries.body:
Lots of catching up to do! We arrived at the Spit in Southport on Sun Jan 11, after a fun weekend at Dux anchorage, on northern South Stradbroke, where we met members of the Southport Yacht Club. Saw lots of wallabies there, beautiful beach with perfect sand dunes. We were appalled when we first dropped the hook in Southport, high rise buildings dotting the skyline. But the Spit was very pretty, with the beach right next to the boat and the ocean not far away. And there were kid boats!

We really enjoyed Manuhiri, a Kiwi ferro boat with Shawn, Angie and their kids Alex, Rory, and Nikki. Brian became special buddies with all 3 of them. Silent Sound, Canadian with Ray, Stella, boys Bradley & Harry, stayed for a month. Brian and Bradley became quite good friends and made up a game together.

Then there were the Aussie boats. La Passorala with Les, Colleen, Jordan & Amy. Keemar III with Bruce, Robin, Jackson & Ryan, 2 big goofy boys that Brian had a lot of fun with. The kids had fires on the beach at night and had a life of their own. I enjoyed watching Brian interact — he has good people skills. Thomas did a lot of wind surfing — figured out water starts and jibes in the flat water behind the sandbars. We enjoyed friendship, happy hours on the beach, lots of swimming & beach walks. Found a small python, called a carpet snake, on the path down to the beach — he would come out at evening, just before sundown. Rick & Mary on Tranquility pulled in and stayed.

It was hard to leave — we felt part of a community for a change. After much agonizing about what to do with our lives, we decided to sail directly back to the U.S., unless plans change of course! So, it is time to move on and we are on our way back to Mooloolaba, to take care of some things, provision, and then on to the Great Barrier Reef. We have enjoyed the fantastic weather, sand and surf of Australia, and Aussie English sounds normal to us now!
entries.conditions: Catch-up entry: Southport Spit stay from mid-January; departing north toward Mooloolaba / GBR.
